name: crdt-text-simulator
description: Two collaborative text replicas on an RGA CRDT: diverge, sync, converge, live in the browser

paragraphs: Two text editors on one page, both free to type at once. Let them diverge, then press Sync now and watch every operation travel between the replicas until both show exactly the same text. Under the hood it is a Replicated Growable Array (RGA), the same family of algorithm that powers collaborative editors like Figma's multiplayer mode and Google Docs style merging.

"Real-time collaboration" looks like magic until you meet the two impossible questions underneath it: what happens when two people type at the same spot at the same time, and what happens when one person deletes a letter that another person is typing next to? Conflict-free Replicated Data Types answer both with clever ordering instead of locking, and this playground lets you cause the conflicts yourself and watch the resolution happen. It is also a genuinely correct CRDT: the fuzz tests hammer it with hundreds of concurrent random edits and assert that every replica converges to identical…
The banner always tells you the truth about the state: how many operations each replica holds that the other has never seen, and whether the texts currently agree.
